model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route): NI to ordinary shareholders less CET1 and associate retention, net debt zero, per-ADS

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case revenue path average (years 1-10); equity CAGR rejected (see warning) and 5yr revenue/EPS CAGRs start from the FY2020 COVID/zero-rate trough
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (0.4-1.9%) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (6.3-9.7%) and EPS (17-45%) CAGRs. Cause: $30bn+ of buybacks FY22-FY25 plus a 50%+ payout keep ordinary equity flat while per-share earnings compound, and FY2020 is a rate/credit trough that inflates every 5yr CAGR. Neither series is a forward growth rate; the base case uses management's revenue target (positive growth rising to 5% in 2028).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are null: bank OCF/FCF is meaningless (deposit and trading-balance flows). SBC is ~0.9% of revenue and stable, so the SBC adjustment does not distort growth.

scenario_narratives.base: HSBC delivers the bottom of its 17%+ RoTE target through 2028. Banking NII holds around $46bn as the structural hedge reinvests at higher yields while policy rates drift lower; wealth fees in Hong Kong and IWPB grow high single digits; the $1.8bn of simplification saves and Hang Seng synergies keep cost growth near 1-2%. ECL runs ~45bp in 2026 with Hong Kong CRE still bleeding, then normalises to 35-40bp. CET1 is held at ~14% and roughly 70-80% of earnings go out as the 50% dividend plus quarterly buybacks. After 2028 returns fade to ~16% as the rate tailwind is competed away and trade-finance share continues to leak to Standard Chartered and Citi.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 19% RoTE (ex notables) printed in 1H26 is the new normal rather than a peak. Hong Kong's super-connector role and cross-border wealth flows drive Asia wealth and insurance growth; wholly-owned Hang Seng delivers the full $0.9bn synergy opportunity; UK ring-fencing reform frees capital and lending capacity; HK CRE losses are cleared through portfolio sales and ECL drops to ~30bp. Revenue grows 6-7% for three years and RoTE settles near 19%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The two concentrations bite together. Faster rate cuts across USD/HKD and GBP compress banking NII as the hedge rolls off, while a mainland China slowdown and tariff-driven trade contraction push Hong Kong CRE, mainland-linked corporate and trade exposures into a credit cycle: ECL near 1% of loans in year 2 and revenue down 2%. US-China sanctions friction raises compliance costs and constrains the cross-border model, and legacy litigation (Madoff/Herald appeals) recurs. Returns recover only to ~13% RoTE, roughly the pre-2022 franchise economics plus the simplification savings.

valuation_philosophy.summary: HSBC is valued as the cash its ordinary shareholders can actually take out: NI to ordinary (after AT1 coupons and the now-small NCI) less the CET1 needed to keep the ratio at 14.1% as the balance sheet grows, less undistributed associate (BoCom/SAB) earnings, discounted at a 10.5% USD cost of equity. Deposits are funding, not debt, so net debt is zero and nothing is deducted after the flows. Value is reported per NYSE ADS (5 ordinary shares).
key_risks_to_valuation: Hong Kong/mainland China CRE: $6.3bn stage-3 HK CRE at end-2025; a deeper cycle is the main driver of the bear case
Rate sensitivity: banking NII guidance is conditioned on mid-July 2026 market rates; the structural hedge tailwind reverses in a fast cutting cycle
US-China geopolitical/sanctions risk to the cross-border model
Notable items recur nearly every period (BoCom impairment/dilution, disposal losses on exits, litigation): the model's underlying margin assumes they average small
BoCom carrying value: the 2.0%-of-revenue associate retention charge is a judgment; full retention would lower value ~3%
Data gap: 1H26 interim not yet in core_metrics; anchors read directly from the SEC 6-K

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 64.65-107.92; ADS parity cross-checked against 0005.HK and HSBA.L
data_sources.financials: HSBC Annual Reports FY2014-FY2025 (research/HSBC/Extracted), HSBC_Metrics.csv; 2026 Interim Results 6-K (SEC, filed 2026-08-04, accession 0001654954-26-007212); Total Voting Rights 6-K 2026-09-30; buy-back 6-Ks 2026-08-05 and 2026-09-28

inputs.share_count_basis: ADS-EQUIVALENTS, not ordinary shares: 1 NYSE ADS = 5 ordinary shares. 17,141.9M ordinary shares in issue at 29-Sep-2026 (Total Voting Rights 6-K 2026-09-30; no treasury shares; after the $1bn Aug-Sep buy-back concluded 2026-09-26, 48.7M shares cancelled) + 103M dilutive potential ordinary shares (1H26 interim: 17,267M diluted vs 17,164M basic at 30-Jun-2026) = 17,244.9M fully diluted / 5 = 3,449.0M ADS. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed inside the flow; buybacks are the distribution of the flow, value-neutral.
inputs.ads_parity_check: 2026-10-02 closes: 0005.HK HK$149.5 x HKDUSD 0.1274 x 5 = $95.23; HSBA.L 1,442.2p x GBPUSD 1.324 x 5 = $95.47; NYSE ADS $96.14. Parity holds within 1%, confirming the 5:1 ratio.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 2026-06-30 = FY2025 cash-flow 'Share-based payment expense' 621 (HSBC_Annual_FY2025.txt:21852) - 1H25 315 + 1H26 319 (2026 Interim Results 6-K 2026-08-04, cash flow statement). Bank: last_fcf is NI to ordinary shareholders (TTM 24,218), reported_fcf = NI + SBC.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 buybacks $9.1bn; paused Jan-2026 for the Hang Seng privatisation; resumed with $1bn announced 2026-08-04 (completed 2026-09-26, 48.66M shares for $998m). Dividend $0.10 per ordinary share per quarter in 2026 interim pattern; target payout 50% of EPS ex material notable items.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 10.5% in USD (HSBC reports and is quoted in USD): 10y UST ~4.2% + beta ~1.05 x 5.25% ERP = ~9.7%, plus ~0.75pp for Hong Kong/mainland China concentration and US-China sanctions/geopolitical exposure that US peers (WFC/USB at 10.0%) do not carry; same as TFC (10.5%). One rate across all three scenarios: risk is carried in the bear path and weight, not a per-scenario premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: bank FCFE flow is after all operating costs including occupancy and IFRS-16 depreciation/interest; no lease adjustment.
inputs.nci_treatment: Inside the flow. 'ebitda' = PBT + SBC - pre-tax equivalent of (AT1 coupons + NCI), so the flow is NI to ORDINARY shareholders. TTM AT1 coupons 1,269 (FY25 1,183 - 1H25 547 + 1H26 633), NCI 524 (FY25 846 - 1H25 384 + 1H26 62). NCI collapses from 2026 because the $13.7bn Hang Seng privatisation (completed 26-Jan-2026) derecognised $7.0bn of NCI; AT1 coupons rise ~$0.1-0.2bn on $4bn issued Mar/May-2026 less $1bn redeemed. AT1 par ($20.7bn) is therefore NOT also deducted in a bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, net_debt = 0, as instructed and as the house precedent for large banks (WFC, USB, TFC, HBAN, NAB.AX). SKILL.md routes banks to residual income on tangible book; FCFE-at-CoE with a CET1-retention charge is the same economics (value = TCE + PV of returns above CoE) expressed as distributable cash. Deposits ($1.83tn customer accounts) are operating funding, not debt; OCF is meaningless (CSV OCF swings -21bn to +182bn). Engine mapping: revenue = net operating income before ECL (CSV definition), TTM to 2026-06-30 = FY25 68,274 - 1H25 34,122 + 1H26 37,742 = 71,894. 'ebitda' = PBT 33,619 (29,907 - 15,810 + 19,522) + SBC 625 - (AT1 1,269 + NCI 524)/(1 - 22.6%) 2,317 = 31,927 (44.4%). FY0 check: (31,927 - 625) x (1 - 22.63%) = 24,218 = reported NI to ordinary. TTM is depressed by ~$2.5bn pre-tax of notable items (H2-25 Madoff/Herald $1.1bn provision, restructuring, disposal losses; 1H26 $0.9bn Malta HFS loss, restructuring, UK Life FX recycling), so year 1 steps up to the underlying level. 'capex' = (a) CET1 retention to hold CET1/revenue at 1.778 (14.1% x RWA 906,417 = 127,805 / 71,894) as revenue grows: 177.8 x g/(1+g), floored at zero; plus (b) 2.0% of revenue for undistributed associate earnings (share of associates $2.9bn/yr, mostly BoCom 19% and SAB 31%; BoCom pays ~30%, so ~$1.8bn/yr is retained in entities HSBC cannot distribute from, and the BoCom stake is partly deducted from CET1; 2.0% vs ~2.4% full retention gives modest credit for the stakes' value). CET1 14.1% sits inside the 14-14.5% target, so NO excess-capital credit in the bridge. D&A = 0 (inside opex). DATA GAP: the 2026 Interim Results (6-K 2026-08-04) are NOT in research/HSBC/Extracted or core_metrics (CSV ends FY2025); 1H26 figures here were read directly from the SEC 6-K (accession 0001654954-26-007212) and should be added to core_metrics by the financial-parser. Analysis.json's '2026-Q3' event (PBT -14% YoY, Madoff provision) describes Q3 2025, not Q3 2026 (Q3 2026 is not yet reported at valuation date) and was not used. The ADS fell ~5% on 2026-10-01 (101.18 -> 95.82, mirrored in HK/LSE); cause not established.

bear.margin_rationale: Global rate cuts reverse the structural-hedge tailwind (NII down), a HK/China CRE and trade-tariff credit cycle takes ECL to ~1% of loans in year 2 (~$5.5bn above base), and legacy litigation recurs. Recovery only to 42% margin: terminal RoTE ~13%, the pre-2022 franchise economics with partial credit for simplification. CET1 retention floored at zero in the year-2 contraction (regulators would not permit a capital release in a credit cycle).

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 (Jul-26 to Jun-27) 5.5%: H2-26 ~$37bn (banking NII guided at least $46bn for 2026 vs $22.9bn in 1H26) plus H1-27 ~$39bn against a TTM depressed by H2-25 notable-item revenue losses. Then management's 2026-28 target of growth rising to 5% in 2028, fading to 3% nominal.
base.margin_rationale: Year 1 48.0% gives NI to ordinary ~$27.5bn = ~17% RoTE on ~$163bn average tangible equity, the bottom of the 17%+ 2026-28 target (1H26 ran 19.1% ex notables, but H2 carries heavier costs and ECL guided ~45bp for 2026). Margin edges up to 49% as $1.8bn simplification saves and Hang Seng synergies meet ~1% cost growth, then fades to 48% as structural-hedge tailwind ends and ECL normalises at 35-40bp. Terminal RoTE ~16%.
base.capex_rationale: CET1 retention 177.8 x g/(1+g) holding CET1 at 14.1% of RWA, plus 2.0% of revenue undistributed associate (BoCom/SAB) earnings. Implied distribution ratio ~69% in year 1 and ~80% at terminal, in line with 50% dividend + buybacks.
base.tax_rationale: TTM ETR 22.6% (FY25 22.7%, 1H26 21.5%); 23% reflects UK bank surcharge, HK 16.5%, Pillar Two top-ups.

bull.margin_rationale: 1H26's 19% RoTE ex notables proves durable: wealth fees compound (Asia net new invested assets), rates stay higher for longer, HK CRE losses roll off and ECL returns to ~30bp, synergies land in full. RoTE ~18.5-19.5% sustained.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (up from the 15% default): earnings rest on one geography (Hong Kong/mainland China ~half of profit) with live CRE stress and US-China sanctions exposure, and NII is explicitly rate-dependent. Base 50%: guidance has been met or raised twice in 2026. Bull 25% (down from 35%): 1H26 RoTE is already above target, so the bull needs peak-cycle returns to persist rather than improve.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
